items.title: Anthropic Lets MCP Servers Ship Skills as Tasks and Elicitation Go GA
items.summary: On Nov 24 Anthropic opened Skills over MCP to public beta in Claude and Claude Code, letting an MCP server distribute step-by-step playbooks and best practices alongside its tools, loaded only when needed and updated centrally with the server. Shopify is using them for store design, HubSpot for customer onboarding and Atlassian for organisational-context work. Two protocol features reached general availability: Tasks, which runs long background jobs and agent loops while Claude continues working, and Elicitation, which pauses for user confirmation before risky actions such as GitHub repository deletion or Supabase charges. File Uploads is coming next. Anthropic reports more than 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and over 10,000 Claude connectors.
items.impact: The agent toolchain is standardising beyond tool calls into instructions, asynchronous work and human checkpoints - useful for teams wiring agents into enterprise systems. Because the features live in the open MCP spec, compatible servers work in any client. The flip side is provenance: centrally updated skills execute inside agent workflows, so they need the same vetting as software dependencies.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Open-Source Shirudo for Live, Reboot-Free Linux Shields
items.summary: On Nov 23 OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source runtime that uses eBPF to block exploit paths on running Linux systems while permanent patches are tested and rolled out. Shields are narrowly scoped so legitimate traffic using the same kernel operations keeps working; they can be observed before enforcement and deployed without restarting services. Shields must be cryptographically signed and pass the Linux eBPF verifier, with TPM-backed records of loading and removal. In a controlled test, a Codex-generated shield added input checks to Java's Base64 decoder and stopped a Java4Shell exploit against a live Elasticsearch service with no restart. The code is BSD 2-Clause; BPF programs carry BSD/GPL dual licensing.
items.impact: It targets the expensive gap between disclosure and a verified patch, especially for always-on inference servers that cannot be rebooted. Letting agents draft shields accelerates response but concentrates trust in signed artefacts and human approval; the project is pre-release, and a shield is containment, not a fix.

items.title: CIA and ODNI Discover Intrusion into Unclassified Open-Source Intelligence Network
items.summary: US intelligence agencies discovered a cyber intrusion involving a network used to mine publicly available, unclassified material for intelligence insights, The New York Times reported on Nov 24, with AP and Reuters confirming further details. Some unclassified information was exposed, and officials said data held by other government agencies may also have been affected. ODNI said there were 'no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems' and that the issue had been resolved. The attacker has not been identified and the entry route remains unknown. The disclosure follows separate breaches at the FBI's National Crime Information Center and the Agriculture Department, though no link between the incidents has been established.
items.impact: Unclassified does not mean harmless: an OSINT platform reveals what analysts collect, which queries they run and which commercial feeds they rely on - a map of agency priorities without a single secret document. For contractors and data vendors, it underlines that access keys on low-sensitivity networks deserve zero-trust controls.

items.title: CISA Adds Actively Exploited MONAI Label and N-able Mail Assure Flaws to KEV
items.summary: On Nov 23 CISA added two vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-133968 is a path traversal flaw (CVSS 9.8) in Project MONAI's MONAI Label, an open-source medical-imaging annotation server that can let an unauthenticated attacker write files outside the datastore and achieve remote code execution. Amazon reported that a suspected China-nexus operator used the open-source CAIRN AI framework to find and exploit the flaw in roughly 11 minutes, then dropped a reverse shell in sitecustomize.py to gain root. CVE-2026-134624 is a CVSS 9.3 server-side request forgery flaw in N-able Mail Assure (SpamExperts) tied to a Nov 16 service disruption. Federal agencies must remediate by Nov 26 under BOD 26-04.
items.impact: The two listings turn an AI-agent capability demo into a compliance deadline: federal agencies and healthcare research networks must patch or document exceptions on a fixed schedule. The 11-minute discovery-to-shell timeline shows why multi-day patch cycles are inadequate for internet-facing research tools that ship without authentication.

items.title: Gatwick AutoPay Breach Exposes Drivers' Credentials, Addresses and Travel Times
items.summary: London Gatwick confirmed on Nov 24 that AutoPay, the third-party system used to charge drivers automatically in its drop-off zones, had been accessed without authorisation. Operator Times24 UK discovered the intrusion; Gatwick disabled AutoPay, emailed affected customers and notified the UK Information Commissioner's Office. Exposed data includes AutoPay login credentials, names, email and home addresses, registered vehicle details, drop-off times and transaction records; in isolated cases the card brand, last four digits and expiry date were also exposed. Full card numbers and security codes were not reported as affected. The number of customers, intrusion window and entry method remain undisclosed, and no group has claimed responsibility.
items.impact: For drivers, reused passwords and the combination of home address with travel times create account-takeover and burglary risk, not just card fraud. For operators, it shows that parking and drop-off systems are identity and payment systems in practice, and that a brand stays accountable when a little-known supplier is breached.
